newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: MINISTER JOSTLED AT UNI
Aboriginal Affairs Minister John Herron didn't get quite the reception he hoped for when he delivered a lecture on the government's plan for Aboriginal communities.
The Minister was heckled and jostled by protestors outside a lecture theatre at the Australian National University in Canberra today.
About 20 protestors, who accused the Government of racism, also tried to prevent Senator Herron's car from leaving the campus after the lecture.

The lecture outlined the Government's plan for greater economic independence for Aboriginal people .. and a proposed pilot program using the Army to improve water and sewerage services in remote communities.
MINERS INTERVIEWED OVER FATAL ACCIDENT
Miners working at the site of yesterday's fatal accident at the Gretley Colliery are being interviewed to try to shed some light on how the tragedy occurred.
Investigators from the Mineworkers Union are speaking with people near the accident site before and at the time of the tunnel collapse which killed four men.
Union check inspector, Jack Tapp, has confirmed that water flowed into the tunnel from a known disused mineshaft, killing the miners.
AIR TRAVEL SET TO RISE IN PRICE
Airline passenger ticket prices look like rising as airlines try to offset the impact of rising fuel prices on their margins.
Qantas and Ansett say they're both closely monitoring the issue.
Qantas has already advised customers it's placing surcharges on its freight rates, to take effect next week.
But it says this represents only a partial recovery of costs which have risen throughout the year in line with rises in the price of crude oil.
Qantas says it's waiting on recommendations from the International Air Transport Association, which has been meeting on the issue in Geneva, before it decides whether to raise passenger prices.
GOVT TO SUPPORT "REASONABLE" PAY INCREASE
The Federal Government will support a pay rise for low income workers.
Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith says the Government is opposed to Labor's inflationary claim, but it will support a reasonable increase.
Mr Reith made the announcement after addressing a conference of union members in Melbourne.
He says further details will be contained in the Government's submission to the Living Wage case.
CLAIMS THE GOVT WIMPED ON NUCLEAR VOTE
The Federal Government is under fire for failing to vote in the UN General Assembly on negotiations towards a nuclear weapons convention.
Australia abstained on the resolution which was introduced by Malaysia, welcoming the International Court of Justice decision in June, that the use or threat of use of nuclear weapons is illegal.
Friends of the Earth's nuclear campaigner, John Hallam, says he's shocked and disappointed that the Australian government said other steps could be taken before a convention takes place.
MOLLER JAILED FOR CONTEMPT OF ROYAL COMMISSION
A former Sydney police officer has been jailed for eight months for being in contempt of the Wood Royal Commission.
27-year old Clinton Moller was arrested in New Zealand and pleaded guilty to contempt, after failing to answer a summons to appear before the inquiry last January.
Supreme Court Justice Dunford said Moller didn't appear before the Royal Commission because he was reluctant to implicate himself and fellow officers in criminal conduct.
The former Bondi officer is awaiting trial on charges of supplying drugs to which he has pleaded not guilty.
THREE DIE IN AIR CRASH
Three people have been killed in a plane crash near Queanbeyan, in south eastern New South Wales.
The plane crashed about five kilometres from the township of Bungendore shortly after taking off from a property.
When emergency crews arrived the plane was engulfed in flames.
Meanwhile, the pilot of a crop-duster has died in a crash at Ebor, west of Coffs Harbour.
The accident happened in dense forest four kilometres north of Point Lookout, in the New England Wilderness area.
GAY COUPLE WIN HEALTH FUND CASE
The Supreme Court in Sydney has rejected an appeal by a health fund not to grant family membership to a gay couple.

Andrew Hope and William Brown went to the Equal Opportunity Tribunal, alleging the NIB Fund had discriminated against them, when it refused them membership at the concessional family rate. They've been living at Newcastle since 1990 with Mr Hope's son from a previous marriage.
The Tribunal found in favour of the couple, but the fund appealed.
Today, Justice McInerney upheld the original decision, ordering that the couple be offered membership at the family rate and be paid 15-hundred dollars in compensation.
